- A cluster with x86 nodes. The images are `linux/amd64` only, so every pod has the node selector
 `kubernetes.io/arch=amd64`.
- An Ingress controller. The defaults match ingress-nginx.
- A default StorageClass, for the bundled Postgres and object store.
- cert-manager with a `ClusterIssuer`, for automatic TLS.
- A clone of the repository, `helm`, and `openssl`.

records.title: Helm chart
records.heading: Generate the instance secrets
records.text:
The chart does not generate secrets. Generate the same set the VM installer makes, from the clone:

git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/alethialabs-io/alethialabs.git && cd alethialabs
(umask 077; : > secrets.env; . deploy/selfhost/secrets.sh; fill_required_secrets secrets.env >/dev/null)

records.title: Helm chart
records.heading: Write a values file
records.text:
DOMAIN=alethia.example.com
(umask 077; . ./secrets.env; {
 echo "domain: $DOMAIN"
 echo "postgres: { password: \"$ALETHIA_DB_PASSWORD\", appPassword: \"$ALETHIA_APP_DB_PASSWORD\" }"
 echo "objectStore: { accessKey: \"$ALETHIA_STORAGE_ACCESS_KEY_ID\", secretKey: \"$ALETHIA_STORAGE_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY\" }"
 echo "secrets:"
 echo " cliJwtSecret: \"$CLI_JWT_SECRET\""
 echo " betterAuthSecret: \"$BETTER_AUTH_SECRET\""
 echo " extraEnv:"
 echo " NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL: \"https://$DOMAIN\""
 echo " BETTER_AUTH_URL: \"https://$DOMAIN\""
 grep -vE '^(CLI_JWT_SECRET BETTER_AUTH_SECRET)=' secrets.env sed -E 's/^([A-Z0-9_]+)=(.*)$/ \1: "\2"/'
} > alethia-values.yaml)

`secrets.extraEnv` becomes environment variables of the console and the runner. Add OAuth and
email keys there too: see [Configuration](/self-host/configuration) and [Email](/self-host/email).

records.title: Helm chart
records.heading: Install the chart
records.text:
helm install alethia deploy/helm/alethia \
 --namespace alethia --create-namespace \
 -f alethia-values.yaml

Then point your domain's DNS record at the Ingress controller's external address.

 
 

Keep `secrets.env` and `alethia-values.yaml` in a secret store, and delete them from disk.

records.title: Helm chart
records.heading: Check that it worked
records.text:
kubectl -n alethia get pods

The console, docs, runner, Postgres and SeaweedFS pods are `Running`. The console pod ran two init
containers first: `wait-for-postgres` and `migrate`. Open `https:// ` and sign in. Until email
is set up, the sign-in code is in the console's log: `kubectl -n alethia logs deploy/alethia-alethia-console`. Resources are named
` -alethia- `.

records.title: Helm chart
records.heading: Use a managed database or object store
records.text:
Turn off the bundled services and point the chart at yours:

helm install alethia deploy/helm/alethia -f alethia-values.yaml \
 --set postgres.enabled=false \
 --set postgres.host=db.internal --set postgres.user=alethia --set postgres.database=alethia \
 --set objectStore.enabled=false \
 --set objectStore.endpoint=https://s3.eu-central-1.amazonaws.com

`postgres.password` is the schema owner's password. `migrate` creates the `alethia_app` role with
`postgres.appPassword`. For a managed store, set `ALETHIA_STORAGE_ACCESS_KEY_ID` and
`ALETHIA_STORAGE_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` in `secrets.extraEnv` to that store's credentials.

To manage the Kubernetes Secret yourself, set `secrets.existingSecret= `. It must hold
`ALETHIA_DATABASE_URL`, `ALETHIA_APP_DATABASE_URL`, `ALETHIA_APP_DB_PASSWORD`,
`ALETHIA_STORAGE_ENDPOINT`, `CLI_JWT_SECRET`, `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET` and every key you would put in
`extraEnv`.

records.title: Helm chart
records.heading: Upgrade
records.text:
helm upgrade alethia deploy/helm/alethia --reuse-values --set image.tag= 

The `migrate` init container runs on every rollout, so the schema moves before the new console
serves. Back up the database first; see [Upgrade and back up](/self-host/upgrading#what-to-back-up).

records.title: Helm chart
records.heading: Key values
records.text:
Value Default What it does 
 --- --- --- 
 `domain` `alethialabs.io` The Ingress host. Always set it. 
 `image.tag` `latest` One tag for every Alethia image. 
 `nodeSelector` `kubernetes.io/arch: amd64` Set to `{}` once multi-arch images exist. 
 `postgres.enabled`, `objectStore.enabled` `true` `false` uses your own service. 
 `ingress.className` `nginx` The Ingress class. 
 `ingress.trustedIpHeader` `x-real-ip` The client-IP header the Ingress overwrites. 
 `ingress.tls.clusterIssuer` `letsencrypt-prod` The cert-manager issuer. 

With another Ingress controller, set `ingress.trustedIpHeader` to a single-value header that
controller overwrites with the client address. In production, sign-in answers `503` when the header
is missing or invalid.

records.title: Helm chart
records.heading: Related
records.text:
- [Configuration](/self-host/configuration): every key you can add to `extraEnv`.
- [Scaling out](/self-host/scaling-out): run more console replicas.

records.title: Self-host
records.text: Self-host. Run the whole Alethia platform on your own VM or Kubernetes cluster, then configure, upgrade and back it up.

records.title: Self-host
records.text:
A self-hosted Alethia is one Docker Compose bundle: the console, the docs, Postgres, an
S3-compatible object store (SeaweedFS), a runner, and Caddy for HTTPS. It runs on a VM in any cloud
or on your own hardware, and needs no managed database or object store.

records.title: Self-host
records.heading: Choose how to install
records.text:
Path Use it when Page 
 --- --- --- 
 Installer You have a Linux VM and a domain. One command. [Install on a VM](/self-host/install) 
 One-click You want AWS or Azure to create the VM from a template. [One-click deploy](/self-host/one-click) 
 OpenTofu You want the VM, its firewall and a Cloudflare Tunnel as code. [OpenTofu per cloud](/self-host/terraform) 
 Helm You already run Kubernetes. [Helm chart](/self-host/helm) 

The one-click templates run the same installer. The Helm chart deploys the same images.

records.title: Self-host
records.heading: Then
records.text:
1. [Configure](/self-host/configuration) sign-in providers, storage and the client-IP header.
2. [Set up email](/self-host/email), so sign-in codes reach your users.
3. [Upgrade and back up](/self-host/upgrading) on a schedule.

Optional: [turn on Enterprise](/self-host/enterprise-setup), [run more console
replicas](/self-host/scaling-out), or [run a managed runner
fleet](/self-host/managed-provisioning) that provisions into your users' clouds.

records.title: Self-host
records.heading: What is in the bundle
records.text:
Service Role 
 --- --- 
 `app` The console: web app and API 
 `preflight` Checks that every instance secret is set and is not a placeholder, then exits 
 `migrate` Applies database migrations, then exits. `app` starts after it. 
 `docs` These docs, at `/docs` 
 `blog` News and changelog, at `/news` 
 `postgres` The database 
 `seaweedfs` Object storage for OpenTofu state and plan files 
 `runner` Runs plan and apply jobs, with the credentials you give it 
 `caddy` The only service with open ports (80 and 443). Gets TLS certificates. 
 `pgweb` Optional database browser (`tools` profile) 
 `openfga` Optional authorization engine for Enterprise (`enterprise` profile) 

The bundle is AGPL-3.0, except the `ee/` directory. See [Licensing](/editions/licensing).

records.title: Install on a VM
records.text: Install on a VM. Install the self-hosted Alethia bundle on a Linux VM with one command, with automatic HTTPS for your domain.

records.title: Install on a VM
records.text:
Install Alethia on one Linux VM. The installer generates every secret, pulls prebuilt images and
starts the stack.

records.title: Install on a VM
records.heading: Before you begin
records.text:
- A Linux VM with an x86-64 CPU, 2 or more vCPU, 8 GB of memory (4 GB is the minimum) and 25 GB of
 disk. The images are built for `linux/amd64` only.
- `git`, `openssl` and `curl` on the VM. The installer adds Docker and the Compose plugin if they are
 missing.
- A domain whose `A` (or `AAAA`) record points at the VM, and ports 80 and 443 open. Without a
 domain, the console serves plain HTTP on port 80, which is enough for a test.
- Outbound access to `ghcr.io`, `github.com` and the clouds you will deploy into.

records.title: Install on a VM
records.heading: Run the installer
records.text:
curl -fsSL https://get.alethialabs.io/self-host \
 DOMAIN=alethia.example.com ACME_EMAIL=you@example.com sh

The installer clones the repository to `/opt/alethia`, writes `/opt/alethia/.env` with a generated
value for every instance secret, and records `ALETHIA_VERSION=latest`. To pin an image tag, add
`ALETHIA_VERSION= `. To install somewhere else, add `ALETHIA_DIR= `.

records.title: Install on a VM
records.heading: Wait for the stack
records.text:
The installer runs a preflight check, pulls the images and starts the stack. It prints
`Alethia is starting at https://alethia.example.com`. Caddy gets a TLS certificate on the first
request, which can take a minute.

records.title: Install on a VM
records.heading: Sign in
records.text:
Open the URL and sign in with your email. No email provider is set yet, so the console writes the
code to its log instead of sending it:

cd /opt/alethia
docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f deploy/selfhost/docker-compose.selfhost.yml logs app grep '\[email\]'

records.title: Install on a VM
records.heading: Check that it worked
records.text:
cd /opt/alethia
docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f deploy/selfhost/docker-compose.selfhost.yml ps

`app`, `postgres`, `seaweedfs`, `runner`, `docs`, `blog` and `caddy` are `running`. `preflight` and
`migrate` have exited with code 0. In the console, **Runners** lists the bundled runner as online.

If the installer stops with `has an instance secret that is not usable`, it names the variable and
the command that replaces it. Nothing was started.

records.title: Install on a VM
records.heading: Install from a clone instead
records.text:
To read the files first, clone the repository and run the same script:

git clone https://github.com/alethialabs-io/alethialabs.git /opt/alethia
cd /opt/alethia
DOMAIN=alethia.example.com ACME_EMAIL=you@example.com sh deploy/install.sh

Do not start the stack with `docker compose up` before the installer has written `.env`: compose
refuses to start while any instance secret is empty, and names it.

records.title: Install on a VM
records.heading: Related
records.text:
- [Configuration](/self-host/configuration): sign-in providers, storage, and the client-IP header.
- [Email](/self-host/email): send sign-in codes instead of logging them.
- [Upgrade and back up](/self-host/upgrading).

records.title: Keyless cloud connectors
records.text: Keyless cloud connectors. What a self-hosted instance needs so that users can connect AWS, GCP and Azure without keys, and how to rotate the issuer key those clouds trust.

records.title: Keyless cloud connectors
records.text:
Let your users connect AWS, GCP and Azure accounts with no stored key. Each instance is its own
OpenID Connect (OIDC) issuer. A user's cloud trusts that issuer, and Alethia exchanges a short-lived
signed assertion for cloud credentials when it needs them. You do not need a cloud account of your
own. How the trust works on each cloud is in [Security](/concepts/security#the-issuer).

Hetzner, DigitalOcean and Civo are not keyless: the user pastes an API token, which Alethia stores
encrypted. They need nothing on this page.

records.title: Keyless cloud connectors
records.heading: Before you begin
records.text:
- `ALETHIA_OIDC_SIGNING_KEY` is set. The installer generates it.
- `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL` is an `https://` address that the internet can reach. AWS, GCP and Azure
 fetch the issuer's public keys from it.

The issuer is ` /api/oidc`. Its discovery document is at
`/api/oidc/.well-known/openid-configuration`, and its public keys at `/api/oidc/jwks`.

records.title: Keyless cloud connectors
records.heading: Check that the issuer is reachable
records.text:
From a machine outside your network:

curl -fsS https://alethia.example.com/api/oidc/.well-known/openid-configuration
curl -fsS https://alethia.example.com/api/oidc/jwks

Both return JSON. Then open **Connectors** in the console: the AWS, GCP and Azure cards offer
**Connect**.

If the console instead says the instance cannot serve a keyless connect, it names one reason:

 Reason Fix 
 --- --- 
 no issuer signing key Set `ALETHIA_OIDC_SIGNING_KEY`. Run the installer again to generate it. 
 no public URL configured Set `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL`. 
 the URL is not HTTPS Give the instance a domain with TLS. See [Install on a VM](/self-host/install). 
 a private or local address Publish the console on a public address, or use a token cloud or a [self-operated runner](/guides/runners/self-operated) that holds its own cloud credentials.

records.title: Keyless cloud connectors
records.heading: What the user does
records.text:
The user runs a setup script or OpenTofu module in their own account, which trusts your issuer, and
pastes the result into the console. See [Connect AWS](/guides/connectors/aws),
[Connect GCP](/guides/connectors/gcp) and [Connect Azure](/guides/connectors/azure). On Azure the
federated credential names issuer ` /api/oidc`, subject `alethia-connector` and
audience `api://AzureADTokenExchange`.

 
 Every user connection trusts your issuer's URL. If `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL` changes, every user must
 run their setup again.

records.title: Keyless cloud connectors
records.heading: Rotate the issuer signing key
records.text:
The signing key is the trust root for every keyless connection, so rotate it with an overlap:

1. Run the rotation script:

 sh /opt/alethia/deploy/selfhost/rotate-secret.sh ALETHIA_OIDC_SIGNING_KEY
 
 The old key moves to `ALETHIA_OIDC_SIGNING_KEY_PREVIOUS`. The issuer publishes both keys and
 signs with the new one.

2. Wait at least 24 hours, so every cloud refreshes its copy of the keys and every old assertion has
 expired.
3. Delete `ALETHIA_OIDC_SIGNING_KEY_PREVIOUS` from `.env`, and restart the console.

No change is needed in your users' clouds.

records.title: Keyless cloud connectors
records.heading: Related
records.text:
- [Managed provisioning](/self-host/managed-provisioning): run the jobs on a runner fleet you operate.
- [Cloud credentials](/concepts/runner/cloud-credentials): how the runner uses the credentials.

records.title: Managed provisioning
records.text: Managed provisioning. Run a fleet of Hetzner runner VMs that your instance scales by queue depth, so your users' plan and deploy jobs run without a runner of their own.

records.title: Managed provisioning
records.text:
Run the jobs for your users. Your instance creates runner VMs on Hetzner Cloud, each one claims a
job, signs in to the user's cloud with that job's own short-lived credential, runs OpenTofu, and
streams the log and the state back. Users never run a runner.

records.title: Managed provisioning
records.heading: How a job runs
records.text:
1. A user connects a cloud and starts a plan or a deploy.
2. Every 60 seconds the scaler compares the queue with each pool, and creates a Hetzner VM when a
 pool needs one. The VM pulls `ghcr.io/alethialabs-io/runner- ` and registers with a
 one-time token that expires.
3. The runner claims the job. It gets a credential for the user's cloud (keyless on AWS, GCP and
 Azure; the user's API token on Hetzner) and a credential for that job's OpenTofu state. State
 goes through the console; the VM never holds a storage key.
4. The job ends, and the VM takes the next job or is removed. A VM runs one job at a time by
 default.

records.title: Managed provisioning
records.heading: Before you begin
records.text:
- A working install with a public HTTPS address. See [Install on a VM](/self-host/install).
- Keyless connectors working, if you offer AWS, GCP or Azure. See
 [Keyless cloud connectors](/self-host/managed-cloud-connectors).
- A Hetzner Cloud project for the fleet, and an API token for it. Keep it apart from any project a
 user connects.
- Permission to manage the fleet. Pools appear only on a self-managed instance, and no licence
 gates them there.

records.title: Managed provisioning
records.heading: Set the fleet keys
records.text:
Add to `/opt/alethia/.env`, then restart the console:

 Key Default What it does 
 --- --- --- 
 `FLEET_PROVIDER` `manual` `hcloud` turns the fleet on. `manual` turns it off. 
 `HCLOUD_TOKEN` none The fleet project's API token. Required. 
 `ALETHIA_WEB_ORIGIN` `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL` The address the VMs call back to. 
 `HCLOUD_SSH_KEYS` none Hetzner SSH key IDs, comma-separated, for emergency access. 
 `HCLOUD_SERVER_TYPES` `cax21,cpx31` Server types to try, in order. 
 `HCLOUD_IMAGE` `ubuntu-24.04` The VM's operating system image. 
 `FLEET_RUNNER_IMAGE_TAG` `latest` The runner image tag the VMs pull. 
 `FLEET_RUNNER_SLOTS` `1` Jobs one VM runs at the same time. 
 `FLEET_MAX_TOTAL_INSTANCES` none A ceiling on VMs across all pools. 
 `FLEET_BOOT_GRACE_SECONDS` `180` How long a new VM is safe from scale-down.

records.title: Managed provisioning
records.heading: Check the runner images
records.text:
Each cloud you offer needs its runner image at the tag you set:

for c in aws gcp azure hetzner; do
 docker manifest inspect ghcr.io/alethialabs-io/runner-$c:latest >/dev/null && echo "runner-$c OK"
done

records.title: Managed provisioning
records.heading: Create one pool per cloud
records.text:
Open **Runners** in the console and select **Add pool**. Choose the cloud, the number of VMs to keep
warm, the maximum, and the Hetzner locations. The scaler reads pools on every pass, so no restart is
needed. A paused pool gets no new VMs.

records.title: Managed provisioning
records.heading: Check that it worked
records.text:
For each cloud you offer:

1. Connect a test account, and create a project with a small cluster.
2. Run a plan. A server named `fleet- -…` appears in the fleet's Hetzner project, and shows in
 **Runners** as online. The plan finishes with its verification result.
3. Deploy, then destroy. The destroy also deletes the job's OpenTofu state.

records.title: Managed provisioning
records.heading: If something fails
records.text:
Symptom Cause and fix 
 --- --- 
 The VM boots and never registers Its registration token expired during a slow image pull. Raise `FLEET_BOOTSTRAP_TOKEN_TTL_SECONDS` (default `3600`) or `FLEET_BOOT_GRACE_SECONDS`. After 5 failed boots in 30 minutes, the pool pauses itself. 
 The VM cannot pull `runner- ` The tag is not published for that cloud. Repeat the image check. 
 The plan fails to sign in to the cloud The user's setup is missing, or the issuer is not reachable. See [Keyless cloud connectors](/self-host/managed-cloud-connectors#check-that-the-issuer-is-reachable). 
 No VM is created `FLEET_PROVIDER` is not `hcloud`, `HCLOUD_TOKEN` is empty, or the pool is paused or at its maximum.

records.title: Managed provisioning
records.heading: Related
records.text:
- [Run untrusted code on the fleet](/self-host/fleet-sandbox): the container sandbox that bring-your-own charts and IaC need.
- [Runners](/guides/runners): the runners users register themselves.

records.title: One-click deploy
records.text: One-click deploy. Launch the self-hosted Alethia bundle on AWS or Azure from a template button, with no local tooling.

records.title: One-click deploy
records.text:
Create a VM on AWS or Azure from a template. The VM runs the [installer](/self-host/install) on
first boot, so you get the same bundle as every other path.

records.title: One-click deploy
records.heading: Before you begin
records.text:
- An AWS account that can create EC2 instances, security groups and Elastic IPs, or an Azure
 subscription where you can create a resource group.
- An SSH key: an EC2 key pair name on AWS, or a public key on Azure.
- Optional: a domain. Create its DNS record after the deploy, pointing at the public IP the template
 outputs.

Both templates create an x86 VM (AWS `t3.medium`, Azure `Standard_D2s_v5`) running Ubuntu 24.04, with
ports 22, 80 and 443 open.

records.title: One-click deploy
records.heading: Deploy on AWS
records.text:
1. Select **Launch Stack**.
2. Fill in the parameters: `KeyName` is required. `Domain`, `AcmeEmail`, `InstanceType`,
 `AllowedSshCidr` and `VolumeSize` are optional. `AllowedSshCidr` defaults to `0.0.0.0/0`, so
 narrow it to your own address range.
3. Create the stack, and read `PublicIp` from its **Outputs**.

The template is
[`deploy/oneclick/aws-cloudformation.yaml`](https://github.com/alethialabs-io/alethialabs/blob/main/deploy/oneclick/aws-cloudformation.yaml).
From the AWS CLI:

aws cloudformation deploy --stack-name alethia \
 --template-file deploy/oneclick/aws-cloudformation.yaml \
 --parameter-overrides Domain=alethia.example.com AcmeEmail=you@example.com KeyName=my-key \
 --capabilities CAPABILITY_IAM

records.title: One-click deploy
records.heading: Deploy on Azure
records.text:
1. Select **Deploy to Azure**.
2. Fill in `sshPublicKey`, and optionally `domain`, `acmeEmail`, `adminUsername`, `vmSize` and
 `location`.
3. Create the deployment, and read `publicIp` from its **Outputs**.

The template is
[`deploy/oneclick/azure-arm.json`](https://github.com/alethialabs-io/alethialabs/blob/main/deploy/oneclick/azure-arm.json).
From the Azure CLI:

az deployment group create --resource-group alethia-cp \
 --template-file deploy/oneclick/azure-arm.json \
 --parameters domain=alethia.example.com acmeEmail=you@example.com \
 sshPublicKey="$(cat ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub)"

records.title: One-click deploy
records.heading: Add a domain later
records.text:
With the domain left empty, the console serves plain HTTP at the public IP. To add HTTPS, point the
domain's DNS record at the IP, SSH to the VM, set `ALETHIA_DOMAIN`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL` and
`BETTER_AUTH_URL` in `/opt/alethia/.env`, and run `sh /opt/alethia/deploy/install.sh` again.

records.title: One-click deploy
records.heading: Check that it worked
records.text:
Open `http:// ` or your domain. The sign-in page loads. First boot takes a few minutes
while Docker installs and the images pull. Then follow [Sign in](/self-host/install#sign-in).

records.title: One-click deploy
records.heading: Related
records.text:
- [Install on a VM](/self-host/install): what the installer does.
- [Configuration](/self-host/configuration) and [Email](/self-host/email).

records.title: Scaling out
records.text: Scaling out. Run several console replicas of a self-hosted Alethia behind one ingress, with no message broker.

records.title: Scaling out
records.text:
Run more than one console container, for throughput or so that one restart does not take the
console down. The replicas need nothing beyond the bundled Postgres.

records.title: Scaling out
records.heading: Before you begin
records.text:
- A working install. See [Install on a VM](/self-host/install).
- Memory for each extra replica. The Helm chart requests 512 MiB for each; give it more under load.

records.title: Scaling out
records.heading: Add replicas
records.text:
From `/opt/alethia`:

docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f deploy/selfhost/docker-compose.selfhost.yml up -d --scale app=3

Caddy sends requests to every `app` container. On the Helm chart, set `console.replicas` instead.

records.title: Scaling out
records.heading: Why no broker is needed
records.text:
- **Live updates.** Job logs, support messages and runner wake-ups reach the browser over
 Server-Sent Events. Each replica listens to Postgres `LISTEN`/`NOTIFY` itself, so an event written
 through any replica reaches the browsers connected to every replica.
- **Rate limits.** The counters are in Postgres, so all replicas count against the same limit, and a
 restart does not reset them.
- **Stored state.** Every replica uses the same database and object store.

The compose file also defines a `redis` service in the `scale-out` profile. Nothing in the current
release uses it, so do not start it.

records.title: Scaling out
records.heading: Check that it worked
records.text:
docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f deploy/selfhost/docker-compose.selfhost.yml ps app

Three `app` containers are `running`. Open a job's log in two browsers: both show new lines as the
job writes them.

records.title: Scaling out
records.heading: Related
records.text:
- [Helm chart](/self-host/helm)
- [Configuration](/self-host/configuration)

records.title: AWS
records.text: AWS. Provision the control-plane VM on an x86 EC2 instance with OpenTofu, behind a Cloudflare Tunnel, with admin access through SSM.

records.title: AWS
records.text:
Provision an EC2 instance for the control plane with `infra/cp-aws`. It has no open port: web
traffic comes through a Cloudflare Tunnel, and you reach a shell through SSM Session Manager. Read
[OpenTofu per cloud](/self-host/terraform) first.

records.title: AWS
records.heading: What it creates
records.text:
- An EC2 `t3.large` (2 vCPU, 8 GB) running Ubuntu 24.04, with an encrypted 60 GB gp3 root volume and
 IMDSv2 required. It runs in the account's default VPC, with a public IP for outbound traffic only.
- A security group with no inbound rules.
- An IAM role and instance profile with only `AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore`.
- The Cloudflare Tunnel, and proxied CNAME records for the apex and `www`.

At the default region `eu-west-1`, on demand, this costs about $72 a month (Infracost). A
`t3.medium` costs about half, with 4 GB of memory.

records.title: AWS
records.heading: Before you begin
records.text:
- AWS credentials for the target account. Use a short-lived source, such as
 `aws sso login --profile `, instead of an access key.
- The Cloudflare token, zone ID and account ID.

records.title: AWS
records.heading: Apply
records.text:
cd infra/cp-aws
cp backend.hcl.example backend.hcl
cp terraform.tfvars.example terraform.tfvars # cloudflare_*, domain, aws_region
tofu init -backend-config=backend.hcl
tofu plan -out=tfplan
tofu apply tfplan

Variables you may change: `instance_type` (must be x86), `root_volume_size`, `aws_region`.

records.title: AWS
records.heading: Check that it worked
records.text:
Open a shell on the instance. No SSH port is needed:

aws ssm start-session --target 

`/opt/alethia` holds the repository.

records.title: AWS
records.heading: Related
records.text:
- [OpenTofu per cloud](/self-host/terraform)
- [One-click deploy](/self-host/one-click): an AWS VM that starts Alethia on its own.

records.title: Azure
records.text: Azure. Provision the control-plane VM on an x86 Gen2 Azure VM with OpenTofu, behind a Cloudflare Tunnel, with admin access through run-command.

records.title: Azure
records.text:
Provision an Azure VM for the control plane with `infra/cp-azure`. It has no inbound rule: web
traffic comes through a Cloudflare Tunnel, and you run commands through the Azure control plane.
Read [OpenTofu per cloud](/self-host/terraform) first.

records.title: Azure
records.heading: What it creates
records.text:
- A `Standard_D2s_v5` (2 vCPU, 8 GB, x86 Gen2) running Ubuntu 24.04, with a 30 GB StandardSSD OS
 disk, Trusted Launch (secure boot and vTPM), a system-assigned managed identity, and boot
 diagnostics for the Serial Console.
- A resource group, a virtual network and a subnet.
- A network security group with no inbound rules.
- A Standard public IP, for outbound traffic only.
- The Cloudflare Tunnel, and proxied CNAME records for the apex and `www`.

At the default location `westeurope`, on demand, this costs about $90 a month (Infracost).

records.title: Azure
records.heading: Before you begin
records.text:
- An Azure subscription, and Contributor on it. Sign in with `az login` instead of a
 service-principal secret.
- The Cloudflare token, zone ID and account ID.

records.title: Azure
records.heading: Apply
records.text:
cd infra/cp-azure
cp backend.hcl.example backend.hcl
cp terraform.tfvars.example terraform.tfvars # location, cloudflare_*
az login
tofu init -backend-config=backend.hcl
tofu plan -out=tfplan
tofu apply tfplan

Variables you may change: `vm_size` (must be x86 Gen2, for Trusted Launch), `os_disk_size`,
`location`.

records.title: Azure
records.heading: Check that it worked
records.text:
Run a command on the VM, or open its Serial Console:

az vm run-command invoke -g -n alethia-cp --command-id RunShellScript --scripts 'ls /opt/alethia'
az serial-console connect -g -n alethia-cp

records.title: Azure
records.heading: Related
records.text:
- [OpenTofu per cloud](/self-host/terraform)
- [One-click deploy](/self-host/one-click): an Azure VM that starts Alethia on its own.

records.title: GCP
records.text: GCP. Provision the control-plane VM on an x86 Compute Engine instance with OpenTofu, behind a Cloudflare Tunnel, with SSH only through IAP.

records.title: GCP
records.text:
Provision a Compute Engine VM for the control plane with `infra/cp-gcp`. Web traffic comes through a
Cloudflare Tunnel, and SSH is open only to Google's Identity-Aware Proxy (IAP). Read
[OpenTofu per cloud](/self-host/terraform) first.

records.title: GCP
records.heading: What it creates
records.text:
- An `e2-standard-2` (2 vCPU, 8 GB) running Ubuntu 24.04, with a 30 GB `pd-balanced` boot disk,
 Shielded VM (secure boot and vTPM), and its own least-privilege service account.
- A firewall rule that allows SSH only from the IAP range `35.235.240.0/20`.
- An ephemeral external IP, for outbound traffic only.
- The Cloudflare Tunnel, and proxied CNAME records for the apex and `www`.

At the default region `europe-west4`, on demand, this costs about $57 a month (Infracost).

records.title: GCP
records.heading: Before you begin
records.text:
- A GCP project with the Compute Engine and IAP APIs turned on.
- Application Default Credentials: `gcloud auth application-default login`. Do not use a
 service-account key file.
- The Cloudflare token, zone ID and account ID.

records.title: GCP
records.heading: Apply
records.text:
cd infra/cp-gcp
cp backend.hcl.example backend.hcl
cp terraform.tfvars.example terraform.tfvars # gcp_project, gcp_region, gcp_zone, cloudflare_*
tofu init -backend-config=backend.hcl
tofu plan -out=tfplan
tofu apply tfplan

Variables you may change: `machine_type` (must be x86), `boot_disk_size`, `gcp_region`, `gcp_zone`.

records.title: GCP
records.heading: Check that it worked
records.text:
gcloud compute ssh alethia-cp --zone --tunnel-through-iap

`/opt/alethia` holds the repository.

records.title: GCP
records.heading: Related
records.text: - [OpenTofu per cloud](/self-host/terraform)

records.title: Hetzner
records.text: Hetzner. Provision the control-plane VM on a Hetzner Cloud x86 server with OpenTofu, behind a Cloudflare Tunnel, with a data volume for Postgres and object storage.

records.title: Hetzner
records.text:
Provision a Hetzner Cloud server for the control plane with `infra/cp-hetzner`. Web traffic comes
through a Cloudflare Tunnel, and the firewall allows only SSH. Read
[OpenTofu per cloud](/self-host/terraform) first.

 
 This stack is also the one the hosted service runs on. It imports the hosted service's own DNS
 record (`dns-imports.tf`) and carries its email routing, switched off. Remove `dns-imports.tf`
 before you apply it to your zone, or the plan fails.

records.title: Hetzner
records.heading: What it creates
records.text:
- A `cx33` server (x86, 4 vCPU, 8 GB) and a 25 GB volume. Docker's data, so Postgres and the object
 store, live on the volume.
- Delete and rebuild protection on the server and the volume, and `prevent_destroy` in OpenTofu.
- A firewall that allows only SSH (port 22).
- The Cloudflare Tunnel, and proxied CNAME records for the apex and `www`.

At Hetzner's list price this costs about €14 a month: the server €13.10 and the volume €1.19.

records.title: Hetzner
records.heading: Before you begin
records.text:
- A Hetzner Cloud project and an API token for it.
- An SSH public key. SSH is the admin channel on Hetzner.
- The Cloudflare token, zone ID and account ID.

records.title: Hetzner
records.heading: Apply
records.text:
cd infra/cp-hetzner
cp backend.hcl.example backend.hcl
cp terraform.tfvars.example terraform.tfvars # hcloud_token, cloudflare_*, ssh_public_key, domain
tofu init -backend-config=backend.hcl
tofu plan -out=tfplan
tofu apply tfplan

Variables you may change: `server_type` (`cx43` for a busier instance), `data_volume_size`,
`location` (default `fsn1`), `ssh_allowed_cidrs`.

To remove the server later, first apply a change that turns the protections off, then destroy. See
`infra/cp-hetzner/README.md`.

records.title: Hetzner
records.heading: Check that it worked
records.text: ssh root@ ls /opt/alethia

records.title: Hetzner
records.heading: Related
records.text: - [OpenTofu per cloud](/self-host/terraform)

records.title: OpenTofu per cloud
records.text: OpenTofu per cloud. Provision a hardened control-plane VM and a Cloudflare Tunnel on Hetzner, AWS, GCP or Azure with OpenTofu, with no open web ports.

records.title: OpenTofu per cloud
records.text:
Provision the VM for a self-hosted instance as code. Each cloud has an OpenTofu stack in
`infra/cp- /` that creates one x86 VM with no open web port, and a Cloudflare Tunnel that
carries its traffic.

 
 These stacks prepare the VM: Docker, a clone of the repository in `/opt/alethia`, and the tunnel.
 They do not start Alethia, and the self-host bundle does not include the tunnel's connector
 (`cloudflared`). Use them only if you will run `cloudflared` on the VM yourself. Otherwise use the
 [installer](/self-host/install) or the [one-click templates](/self-host/one-click), which serve
 HTTPS directly.

records.title: OpenTofu per cloud
records.heading: Choose a cloud
records.text:
Apply one stack per domain. Two stacks on the same domain fight over its DNS records and tunnel.

 Cloud Stack Default VM Admin access Page 
 --- --- --- --- --- 
 Hetzner `infra/cp-hetzner` `cx33`, 4 vCPU, 8 GB SSH with a key [Hetzner](/self-host/terraform/hetzner) 
 AWS `infra/cp-aws` `t3.large`, 2 vCPU, 8 GB SSM Session Manager [AWS](/self-host/terraform/aws) 
 GCP `infra/cp-gcp` `e2-standard-2`, 2 vCPU, 8 GB SSH through IAP [GCP](/self-host/terraform/gcp) 
 Azure `infra/cp-azure` `Standard_D2s_v5`, 2 vCPU, 8 GB `az vm run-command` and Serial Console [Azure](/self-host/terraform/azure) 

Every VM is x86, because the images are `linux/amd64` only.

records.title: OpenTofu per cloud
records.heading: What every stack does
records.text:
- **No inbound web traffic.** The firewall opens no port 80 or 443. `cloudflared` on the VM dials out
 to Cloudflare, and TLS ends at Cloudflare's edge.
- **Proxied DNS.** The apex and `www` are proxied CNAME records onto ` .cfargotunnel.com`.
 The tunnel sends both to `http://caddy:80` on the VM.
- **Checks in the plan.** Each stack's `checks.tf` fails the plan if the posture regresses, for
 example if a web port opens.

records.title: OpenTofu per cloud
records.heading: Before you begin
records.text:
- A Cloudflare zone, its zone ID and account ID, and an API token with DNS edit and Cloudflare Tunnel
 permissions.
- An S3-compatible bucket for OpenTofu state.
- Credentials for the cloud. Use short-lived ones, such as the cloud CLI's sign-in.
- OpenTofu.

records.title: OpenTofu per cloud
records.heading: Apply a stack
records.text:
cd infra/cp- 
cp backend.hcl.example backend.hcl # the state bucket's endpoint and credentials
cp terraform.tfvars.example terraform.tfvars # domain, cloudflare_* IDs, cloud settings
tofu init -backend-config=backend.hcl
tofu plan -out=tfplan
tofu apply tfplan

Read the plan before you apply it. Then get the tunnel's token, which `cloudflared` needs:

tofu output -raw tunnel_token

The token is a secret. Pass it to `cloudflared` as `TUNNEL_TOKEN`; do not print it into logs.

records.title: OpenTofu per cloud
records.heading: Check that it worked
records.text:
The cloud console shows one VM named `alethia-cp`. In Cloudflare, the tunnel exists and the apex
record points at it. The tunnel shows as healthy once `cloudflared` runs on the VM.

records.title: OpenTofu per cloud
records.heading: Related
records.text:
- [Install on a VM](/self-host/install): start the bundle on the VM.
- [Configuration](/self-host/configuration#domain-and-client-ip): how the console reads the client
 IP address, which a tunnel changes.

records.title: Upgrade and back up
records.text: Upgrade and back up. Back up a self-hosted Alethia bundle, upgrade it to a new image tag, and restore it from a backup.

records.title: Upgrade and back up
records.text:
Back up the three things that hold state, then upgrade by running the installer again. To roll back,
restore the backup: never run an older image against a newer database schema.

The commands on this page run on the VM, from `/opt/alethia`. Define this shortcut first:

cd /opt/alethia
alias dc='docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f deploy/selfhost/docker-compose.selfhost.yml'

records.title: Upgrade and back up
records.heading: What to back up
records.text:
What Why it matters 
 --- --- 
 `.env` Holds the instance secrets. Without `ALETHIA_CRED_ENCRYPTION_KEY`, stored connector secrets cannot be decrypted. Keep this copy somewhere encrypted. 
 Postgres Every project, environment, job and user. 
 The `alethia_seaweedfs-data` volume OpenTofu state and plan files. State cannot be rebuilt, and without it Alethia cannot change or destroy what it created.

records.title: Upgrade and back up
records.heading: Dump the database
records.text:
dc exec -T postgres pg_dump -U alethia -d alethia -Fc > alethia-$(date +%F).dump

Run it from cron every day. It does not stop the console.

records.title: Upgrade and back up
records.heading: Copy the object store
records.text:
Stop the store for a consistent copy, then start it again:

dc stop seaweedfs
docker run --rm -v alethia_seaweedfs-data:/data -v "$PWD":/backup alpine \
 tar czf /backup/seaweedfs-$(date +%F).tgz -C /data .
dc start seaweedfs

records.title: Upgrade and back up
records.heading: Move the copies off the VM
records.text:
Copy `.env`, the dump and the archive to storage outside the VM, such as a bucket in another
account. A cloud snapshot of the VM's disk (EBS snapshots, Hetzner backups) is a second copy, not a
replacement: it restores the whole VM, not one table.

records.title: Upgrade and back up
records.heading: Upgrade
records.text:
1. Take a backup.
2. Run the installer again, with the tag you want:

 curl -fsSL https://get.alethialabs.io/self-host ALETHIA_VERSION= sh
 
 Without `ALETHIA_VERSION`, it keeps the tag recorded in `.env`. With `latest`, each run pulls
 the newest build.

The installer updates the compose files in `/opt/alethia`, adds any new instance secret to `.env`,
and keeps every value already there. The `migrate` service applies the new schema before `app`
starts. Move one minor version at a time.

records.title: Upgrade and back up
records.heading: Check that it worked
records.text:
dc ps

`migrate` has exited with code 0, and `app` is `running`. If `migrate` failed, read
`dc logs migrate`, then restore the backup.

records.title: Upgrade and back up
records.heading: Restore
records.text:
dc stop app runner
dc exec -T postgres pg_restore -U alethia -d alethia --clean --if-exists < alethia- .dump
dc stop seaweedfs
docker run --rm -v alethia_seaweedfs-data:/data -v "$PWD":/backup alpine \
 sh -c 'rm -rf /data/* && tar xzf /backup/seaweedfs- .tgz -C /data'
dc up -d

Restore the `.env` from the same backup first, and set `ALETHIA_VERSION` in it to the tag the backup
was taken on.

records.title: Upgrade and back up
records.heading: Inspect the database
records.text:
dc --profile tools up -d pgweb

pgweb listens on port 8081 of the VM. Reach it through an SSH tunnel; do not open the port.

records.title: Upgrade and back up
records.heading: Related
records.text:
- [Configuration](/self-host/configuration): rotate instance secrets.
- [Changelog](/changelog): breaking changes and upgrade steps.

records.title: Billing and plans
records.text: Billing and plans. Fix a plan or trial that cannot start, a failed payment, and refusals from plan and usage limits.

records.title: Billing and plans
records.text:
Manage plans on the **Billing** page in the console's settings. Prices are on the
[pricing page](https://alethialabs.io/pricing), and each plan's ceilings are in
[Limits](/reference/limits).

records.title: Billing and plans
records.heading: "Alethia is not yet able to sell to customers in this country in this capacity."
records.text:
**Cause:** paid plans open one market at a time, and are not open yet for your country or for the way
you buy (as an individual or for an organization). The pricing page shows which markets are open.

**Fix:** keep using the Hobby plan. It stays free, with no time limit. To hear when your market
opens, write to sales@alethialabs.io.

An organization in an EU country other than Bulgaria that has a VAT number can't be charged yet.
Alethia can give such an organization complimentary Early Access instead: the paid plan with nothing
charged and nothing owed. Billing starts only after the organization agrees to pay, and the free
period is never charged. To ask for it, write to sales@alethialabs.io.

records.title: Billing and plans
records.heading: A purchase asks for more information first
records.text:
The console shows one of these before it starts a purchase:

 Message What to do 
 --- --- 
 "Accept the current Terms of Service before subscribing." Accept the terms when the console asks, then try again. 
 "Tell us whether you are buying as an individual or on behalf of an organization …" Choose one. The two carry different rights. 
 "Add a billing address before subscribing." Add the address on the **Billing** page.

records.title: Billing and plans
records.heading: "Couldn't start the purchase. Billing may not be configured on this deployment"
records.text:
**Cause:** the console could not start the payment. On a self-hosted console, billing is often not
set up at all.

**Fix:** try again. If it continues on alethialabs.io, open a support case from **Support** in the
sidebar.

records.title: Billing and plans
records.heading: The Pro trial is not offered, or is refused
records.text:
Message Cause 
 --- --- 
 "This organization has already used its free Pro trial. …" Each organization gets one trial. 
 "Your account has already used its free Pro trial. …" Each person gets one trial, across every organization. 
 "Too many Pro trials have been started from your network recently, so a new one can't start now. …" Your network reached the trial ceiling in [Limits](/reference/limits). 

**Fix:** you can still subscribe to Pro from the **Billing** page, when paid plans are open for you.

records.title: Billing and plans
records.heading: The trial ended
records.text:
**Cause:** the Pro trial lasts 30 days and needs no card. When it ends without a paid plan, the
organization goes back to the Hobby plan. Alethia sends an email when this happens.

**Fix:** nothing is deleted. Projects, environments, and clusters stay, and the Hobby plan's limits
apply again. To keep Pro, subscribe on the **Billing** page.

records.title: Billing and plans
records.heading: "Payment failed"
records.text:
The **Billing** page shows **Payment failed**: "The last payment for … didn't go through, so this
organization's paid features are paused until a payment succeeds." Alethia also sends an email.

**Cause:** the card was declined, expired, or needs your bank's confirmation.

**Fix:** select **Update the payment method**. If you see "Ask a member with the billing permission
to update the payment method.", ask a member who manages billing.

records.title: Billing and plans
records.heading: "The payment did not complete — the card may have been declined, or your bank may need you to confirm it."
records.text:
**Cause:** the payment for a new organization's plan did not complete. The organization is on the
Hobby plan until it is paid.

**Fix:** confirm the payment with your bank, or try another card. If the console says the payment is
still being confirmed, wait. A bank debit can take several business days.

records.title: Billing and plans
records.heading: A feature says it needs another plan
records.text:
**Cause:** the feature is part of a higher plan. The dialog says which one: "This feature is
available on the … plan."

**Fix:** upgrade on the **Billing** page, or compare plans on the
[pricing page](https://alethialabs.io/pricing).

records.title: Billing and plans
records.heading: Job and minute limits
records.text:
The daily job limit and the monthly provisioning minutes are described in
[Troubleshoot a deploy](/troubleshooting/deploy#the-daily-job-limit-is-reached).

records.title: Bring-your-own charts
records.text: Bring-your-own charts. Fix a bring-your-own Helm chart that stays OutOfSync, Missing or Progressing, fails its sync on a refused kind, or has pods refused by the namespace's admission rules.

records.title: Bring-your-own charts
records.text:
A bring-your-own chart is an ArgoCD Application. Start with its sync result in ArgoCD: Alethia shows
the Application's health and sync status, but not the resource that failed. For how charts run, see
[Bring-your-own charts](/concepts/bring-your-own-charts).

records.title: Bring-your-own charts
records.heading: The Application is OutOfSync, and you changed nothing
records.text:
**Symptom:** the chart stays `OutOfSync` after every sync.

**Cause:** the chart renders a value that differs on each render, such as a generated password, a
timestamp or a self-signed certificate.

**Fix:** pin the value in the chart, usually through an `existingSecret` option.

records.title: Bring-your-own charts
records.heading: The Application is OutOfSync after a change in the cluster
records.text:
**Symptom:** you edited a resource with `kubectl`, and the Application shows `OutOfSync`.

**Cause:** self-heal is off for bring-your-own charts, so ArgoCD leaves your change. A deploy alone
does not revert it.

**Fix:** push a commit to the tracked ref, delete the edited resource so the next sync recreates it,
or sync the Application in ArgoCD.

records.title: Bring-your-own charts
records.heading: The Application is Missing
records.text:
**Symptom:** the Application shows `Missing`.

**Cause:** its resources do not exist. Usually the chart declares a kind the project refuses, or the
chart path does not exist at the configured ref.

**Fix:** read the sync result in ArgoCD. Fix the path or ref, or turn off the refused part of the chart.

records.title: Bring-your-own charts
records.heading: The sync fails and names a kind that is not allowed
records.text:
**Symptom:** the sync result names a resource whose kind is not in the
[allowed list](/concepts/bring-your-own-charts#what-your-chart-may-create).

**Cause:** bring-your-own charts cannot create that kind.

**Fix:** turn that part of the chart off, usually with a value. For a `ServiceAccount`, set
`serviceAccount.create: false` or its equivalent. Or ask for the kind through a support case. If the
chart created objects of that kind before it was refused, they stay, and ArgoCD no longer manages
them. Delete them yourself.

records.title: Bring-your-own charts
records.heading: The sync fails and names an ExternalSecret or SecretStore
records.text:
**Symptom:** the sync result names a kind from `external-secrets.io`.

**Cause:** the chart ships its own secret-sync resource, which bring-your-own charts cannot create.

**Fix:** turn it off, for example with `externalSecret.enabled: false`. Declare a
[binding](/guides/design-project/bring-your-own-charts#bind-a-workload-to-your-infrastructure) on the
chart's workload, and point the chart at the Secret the binding creates.

records.title: Bring-your-own charts
records.heading: A ValidatingAdmissionPolicy denies the request
records.text:
**Symptom:** the sync fails with `ValidatingAdmissionPolicy 'alethia-byo-admission-enforce-…' …
denied request`.

**Cause:** the chart declares an object the namespace refuses, such as a `LoadBalancer` Service. See
[Admission policy](/concepts/chart-admission#admission-policy).

**Fix:** change the value that renders the object, for example `service.type: ClusterIP`.

records.title: Bring-your-own charts
records.heading: A pod violates PodSecurity baseline
records.text:
**Symptom:** a pod is refused with `violates PodSecurity "baseline:v1.33"`.

**Cause:** the pod asks for access to its node. The message names the field. See
[Pod Security](/concepts/chart-admission#pod-security).

**Fix:** turn that part of the chart off, usually with a value.

records.title: Bring-your-own charts
records.heading: The Application stays Progressing
records.text:
**Symptom:** the Application shows `Progressing` and does not finish.

**Cause:** ArgoCD waits for a workload to become ready. A pod stuck `Pending` with
`Insufficient memory` or `Insufficient cpu` asks for more than any node can give.

**Fix:** lower the pod's resource request, or provision a larger node type.

records.title: Bring-your-own charts
records.heading: The chart is not deployed, and the Deploy tab names another chart
records.text:
**Symptom:** the **Deploy** tab says the chart's namespace belongs to another chart.

**Cause:** the chart kept a namespace from before the namespace rules, and that namespace is another
chart's default namespace.

**Fix:** attach the chart again with another namespace, or leave it blank to use `byo- `.

records.title: Cluster access
records.text: Cluster access. Fix a kubeconfig that the CLI or the console will not give you, and a kubectl that says Unauthorized.

records.title: Cluster access
records.text:
Find the message you see, then do what the row says. `alethia cluster kubeconfig` prints errors
after `Error:`. `alethia cluster token` prints them after `alethia cluster token:`, and `kubectl`
shows that line. How cluster access works is in [Cluster access](/concepts/cluster-access).

records.title: Cluster access
records.heading: kubectl says "You must be logged in to the server (Unauthorized)"
records.text:
**Cause:** the credential expired, or someone revoked it.

**Fix:** with a static kubeconfig, run `alethia cluster kubeconfig` again. With an exec kubeconfig,
the cache may still hold a revoked token, for example after someone deleted the `alethia-view`
ServiceAccount. Delete the cache directory (see
[the cache locations](/concepts/cluster-access#exec-and-static-kubeconfigs)), then run `kubectl`
again.

records.title: Cluster access
records.heading: The control plane refuses the request
records.text:
Status Message Fix 
 --- --- --- 
 401 your session is not valid — run `alethia login`, then try again Run `alethia login`. 
 402 your organization's plan does not allow another kubeconfig right now: … The mint uses runner minutes. Run `alethia usage` to see the limit you reached. 
 403 your role cannot mint a kubeconfig for this cluster (owners, admins and operators can) Ask an owner or admin for a role with `cluster:access_readonly`. 
 403 you cannot mint an admin kubeconfig for this cluster: … drop --admin for read-only access Run it without `--admin`. For admin access, sign in as yourself with `alethia login`, or ask for a role with `cluster:access_admin`. 
 404 the cluster was not found in the active organization Run `alethia org switch`, or pass `--org`. 
 409 The cluster has not been provisioned, so there is nothing to mint a kubeconfig for Deploy the environment. Drafts and environments being destroyed cannot get a kubeconfig. 
 422 This cluster's cloud cannot mint a kubeconfig through Alethia The cluster is not on AWS, GCP, Azure or Hetzner. Use the cloud's own CLI. 
 429 too many kubeconfig requests — try again in … You made more than 20 requests in 10 minutes in this org

records.heading: The CLI gives up while it waits
records.text:
Message Fix

 the kubeconfig request expired before a runner completed it … No runner took the job within 10 minutes. Check `alethia runner list`.
